q: 201. The diaphragm of a leveling telescope contains .............
options: two vertical wires and three horizontal wires
three vertical wires and two horizontal wires
two vertical wires and two horizontal wires
explain: A standard diaphragm usually contains one main horizontal cross-hair, two shorter additive horizontal hairs (stadia wires), and two vertical wires for centering.

q: 202. At a change point .............
options: the first reading was taken from the preceding station
the second reading is taken on the staff from the following station
explain: A change point (CP) requires a Fore Sight (FS) from the old instrument position and a Back Sight (BS) from the new instrument position on the same staff location.

q: 203. An inverted level staff is held when .............
explain: Inverted staff readings are taken when the point is above the line of sight, such as the soffit of a tunnel, a ceiling, or the underside of a bridge girder.

q: 204. When the back staff reading and forward staff reading at a station of levelling are the same, their difference shall be entered .............
options: in both rise and fall columns
explain: Technically, if the difference is zero, it represents no change in elevation; in some booking formats, a zero is noted to maintain the continuity of the Rise/Fall calculations.

q: 205. Sensitiveness of a level tube depends upon .............
options: the radius of the curvature of its inner surface
the diameter of the level tube
the length of the vapor bubble
explain: Sensitivity increases with a larger radius of curvature, larger diameter, longer bubble length, and lower viscosity/surface tension of the liquid.

q: 206. Cumulative error that occur in chaining are proportional to .............
explain: Cumulative errors (like incorrect tape length) increase directly with the length of the line (L), whereas compensating errors are proportional to √L.

q: 207. The theodolite is an instrument used for measuring very accurately .............
explain: The primary function of a theodolite is the precise measurement of both horizontal and vertical angles.

q: 208. The process of turning the telescope of a theodolite over its supporting axis through 180° in a vertical plane, is called .............
explain: Transiting, plunging, and reversing are synonymous terms for rotating the telescope 180° around its horizontal (trunnion) axis.

q: 209. An imaginary line joining the point of intersection of the cross-hairs of the diaphragm and the optical plane is called .............
explain: The line of collimation is the line passing through the intersection of the cross-hairs and the optical center of the objective lens.

q: 210. A line joining the optical centre of the object glass and the centre of the eye piece is known as .............
explain: The axis of the telescope is defined as the line joining the optical center of the objective and the center of the eyepiece.

q: 211. In the surveying telescopes, cross hairs are fitted in .............
options: optical centre of the eye piece
explain: The diaphragm containing the cross-hairs is placed in front of the eyepiece so that the image formed by the objective can be viewed simultaneously with the hairs.

q: 212. In the surveying telescope, diaphragm is held .............
explain: The diaphragm is positioned near the eyepiece (at the focal plane of the objective) to ensure the observer sees the cross-hairs superimposed on the target.

q: 213. If the chain line which runs along N-S direction is horizontal and the ground in E-W direction is sloping .............
options: it is possible to set offsets correctly on east side
it is possible to set offsets correctly on east side
it is not possible to set offsets correctly on west side
it is possible to set offsets correctly on both sides
explain: Slope in the transverse direction (perpendicular to the chain line) does not prevent the setting of offsets, though horizontal distances must be measured correctly.

q: 214. Perpendicularity of an offset may be judged by eye, if the length of the offset is .............
explain: Generally, for offsets shorter than 15m, the perpendicular can be estimated by eye without significant loss of accuracy for standard scales.

q: 215. The horizontal equivalent which is a term generally uses in contoured map is .............
options: the least distance between two consecutive contours
the greatest distance between two consecutive contours
the mean distance between two consecutive contours
explain: Horizontal equivalent is the horizontal distance between two consecutive contours; it is smallest where the slope is steepest.

q: 216. A pass or a saddle in a mountainous region .............
options: the lowest point of the ridge lines coincides with the highest point of the valley point
explain: A saddle is a low point on a ridge between two peaks; it typically connects two ridges and two valleys.

q: 217. Which one of the following methods can be used for contour interpolation?
explain: Contour interpolation is done via estimation (rough), arithmetic (precise but slow), or graphical methods (using a tracing sheet).

q: 218. In Indian tangent clinometer is associated with .............
explain: The Indian tangent clinometer is used primarily in Plane Table surveying to determine the elevations of points by measuring vertical angles.

q: 219. The instrument used for accurate centering in plane table survey is .............
explain: A plumbing fork (U-frame) with a plumb bob is used to center the point on the paper exactly over the station on the ground.

q: 220. A Bench mark is a .............
options: the last station where the survey closes
explain: A Bench Mark (BM) is a relatively permanent point of reference whose elevation (RL) is known.

q: 221. The height of instrument is equal to .............
options: reduced level of bench mark + back sight
reduced level of bench mark + fore sight
reduced level of bench mark + intermediate sight
explain: Height of Instrument (HI) = RL of the point + the Back Sight (BS) reading taken on that point.

q: 222. A method of differential leveling is used in order to find the difference in elevation between points when .............
options: the difference in elevation between them is too great
explain: Differential leveling (fly leveling) is employed when points are far apart, obstructed, or have a large elevation difference requiring multiple setups.

q: 223. The collimation method for obtaining the reduced levels of points does not provide a check on .............
explain: In the HI (Collimation) method, there is no arithmetic check for the calculation of RLs of Intermediate Sights (IS).

q: 224. The rise and fall method for obtaining the reduced levels of points provides a check in .............
explain: The Rise and Fall method provides a complete check on all readings, including Intermediate Sights.

q: 225. Collimation method is use in .............
explain: The Collimation (HI) method is widely used for profile leveling (due to many intermediate sights) and differential leveling.

q: 226. The method of leveling in which the heights of mountains are found by observing the temperature at which water boils is known as .............
explain: Hypsometry determines elevation by measuring the boiling point of water, which decreases as atmospheric pressure (and thus altitude) changes.

q: 227. Which of the following statement is correct?
options: in leveling the effect of curvature is to decrease the staff reading
the effect of refraction in leveling is to increase the staff reading
the combined effect of curvature and refraction in leveling is to increase the staff reading
explain: Curvature makes objects appear lower (increasing staff reading), while refraction makes them appear higher (decreasing staff reading). The combined effect is an increase in the staff reading.

q: 228. In leveling, the effect of refraction may be taken as ............. of that due to curvature.
explain: Refraction correction is generally taken as 1/7th of the curvature correction and is opposite in sign.

q: 229. In leveling, the correction for curvature (in meters) is equal .............
explain: The curvature correction is given by the formula Cc = 0.07849 D², where D is the distance in kilometers.

q: 230. In leveling, the correction for combined curvature and refraction (in metres) is equal to .............
explain: The combined correction C = 0.0673 D² accounts for both the earth's curvature and atmospheric refraction.

q: 231. The error which is not completely eliminated in reciprocal levelling is .............
options: error due to non-adjustment of the line of collimation
error due to non-adjustment of bubble tube
explain: While reciprocal leveling eliminates curvature and collimation errors, refraction errors may not be fully eliminated if atmospheric conditions change between observations.

q: 232. The contour interval depends upon the .............
explain: Contour intervals are chosen based on the steepness of terrain, the map scale, and the required precision for the project's purpose.

q: 233. In direct method of contouring, the process of locating or identifying points lying on a contour called .............
explain: Vertical control is the process used to find points of the same elevation (the contour line) using a level and staff.

q: 234. In an internal focusing type of telescope, the lens provided is .............
explain: Internal focusing telescopes use a double concave (diverging) lens mounted between the objective and the diaphragm.

q: 235. Which of the following can be neutralized by setting the level midway between the two stations?
options: Error due to both curvature and refraction
explain: By equalizing the Back Sight and Fore Sight distances, the errors from curvature, refraction, and imperfect collimation are canceled out.

q: 236. In any closed traverse, if they survey work is correct, then .............
options: the algebraic sum of latitudes should be equal to zero
the algebraic sum of departures should be equal to zero
the sum of northings should be equal to the sum of southings
explain: For a closed traverse, the sum of latitudes (Northings - Southings) and departures (Eastings - Westings) must both equal zero.

q: 237. In reciprocal leveling, the error which is not completely eliminated, is due to .............
explain: As atmospheric refraction varies with time and temperature, it is the only error in reciprocal leveling that might not be perfectly canceled.

q: 238. For true difference in elevations between two points A and B, the level must be set up .............
options: at any point between A and B
at the exact midpoint of A and B
explain: Placing the level at the exact midpoint ensures that any instrumental or natural errors are identical for both readings and thus subtract to zero.

q: 239. The most commonly used set of theodolite operations are .............
explain: Face Left (Telescope Normal) combined with a Right Swing is the standard procedure for measuring horizontal angles.

q: 240. Geodetic surveying is different from plane surveying because of .............
options: the large difference of elevations between various points
explain: Geodetic surveying accounts for the Earth's curvature, whereas plane surveying treats the Earth's surface as a flat plane.

q: 241. The error due to bad ranging is .............
explain: Bad ranging always makes the measured line longer than the true length, resulting in a cumulative positive error.

options: ties or check lines which are perpendicular to chain line
sets of minor instruments in chain surveying
chain lines which go out of alignment
explain: Offsets are lateral measurements taken from the main chain line to locate the positions of nearby features.

q: 243. The tension, at which the effects of pull and sag for a tape are neutralised, is known as .............
explain: Normal tension is the specific pull applied to a tape so that the increase in length due to pull equals the decrease in length due to sag.

q: 244. A line joining the apex of a triangle to some fixed point on the opposite side is called a .............
explain: A check line (or proof line) is used to verify the accuracy of the framework by measuring from a known vertex to a point on the opposite side.

q: 245. The included angles of a theodolite traverse, are generally measured .............
explain: In theodolite traversing, it is standard practice to measure angles clockwise from the back station to the forward station.

q: 246. Distance between two neighboring brass rings is .............
explain: In a metric chain, brass rings are typically provided at every 1 meter interval for easy counting.

q: 247. When the image formed by the objective is not situated in the plane of cross-hairs .............
explain: Parallax occurs when the image does not fall on the plane of the cross-hairs; it is removed by properly focusing the objective and eyepiece.

q: 248. When 1 cm on a map represents 10 m on the ground, the representative fraction of the scale is .............
explain: RF = Map Distance / Ground Distance = 1cm / 1000cm = 1/1000.

q: 249. The representative fraction 1/2500 means that the scale is .............
explain: 1/2500 means 1 cm on the map = 2500 cm on the ground. 2500 cm = 25 meters.

q: 250. The main object of running a tie line is .............
options: to check accuracy of the work
to take details of nearby objects
to take offsets for detailed surveying
explain: Tie lines are primarily used to pick up internal details of the area that are far from the main chain lines.

q: 251. The main difference between an optical square and prism square is .............
options: that optical square is more accurate than prism square
that no adjustment is required in a prism square since the angle between the reflecting surfaces cannot be changed
explain: While both use the principle of double reflection, the prism square is fixed and requires no adjustment compared to the mirrors in an optical square.

q: 252. Rankine's deflection angle in minutes is obtained by multiplying the length of the chord by .............
options: square of the degree of the curve
inverse of the degree of the curve
explain: Rankine's method relates the deflection angle directly to the chord length and the degree of the curve (or radius).

q: 253. An ideal transition curve is .............
explain: The clothoid (or Euler spiral) is considered the ideal transition curve because its curvature increases linearly with distance.

q: 254. Shift of a curve, is .............
explain: The shift (S) required for a transition curve is calculated using the formula S = L²/24R.

q: 255. In the prismatic compass .............
options: the magnetic needle moves with the box
the line of sight doesn't move with the box
the magnetic needle and graduated circle do not move with the box
explain: In a prismatic compass, the needle and the graduated ring are attached; they remain stationary relative to the magnetic meridian while the box rotates.

q: 256. Local attraction in compass surveying may exist due to .............
options: incorrect leveling of the magnetic needle
loss of magnetism of the needle
friction of the needle at the pivot
presence of magnetic substances near the instrument
explain: Local attraction is caused by external magnetic objects (iron ore, steel structures, power lines) interfering with the Earth's magnetic field.

q: 257. The horizontal angle between true meridian and magnetic meridian at a place is called .............
explain: Magnetic declination is the angle of deviation between the true North and the magnetic North at a specific location.

q: 258. Determining the difference in elevation between two points on the surface of the earth, is known as .............
explain: Leveling is the general branch of surveying used to determine the relative heights (elevations) of points.

q: 259. When the bubble of the level tube of level, remains central .............
options: axis of the telescope is horizontal
geometrical axis of the telescope is horizontal
explain: A centered bubble indicates that the axis of the level tube is horizontal, and if adjusted, the line of collimation will also be horizontal.

q: 260. Plotting of inaccessible points on a plane table, is done by .............
explain: The intersection method allows the surveyor to plot a point by sighting it from two different stations without actually traveling to the point.

q: 261. Locating the position of plane table station with reference to three known points, is known as .............
explain: The three-point problem is a resection technique used to find the location of the instrument station by sighting three known mapped points.

q: 262. The 'fix' of a plane table from three known points, is good, if .............
options: either the right or left station is nearest
explain: A good 'fix' in a three-point problem is achieved when the middle station is closer to the instrument than the other two points.

q: 263. A series of closely spaced contour lines represents a .............
explain: Close contours indicate that the elevation is changing rapidly over a short horizontal distance, signifying a steep slope.

q: 264. Direct method of contouring is .............
explain: The direct method involves physically tracing the contour on the ground; it is very accurate but slow and tedious.

q: 265. The angle of intersection of a counter and a ridge line, is .............
explain: Contour lines cross ridge lines and valley lines at right angles (90°).

q: 266. In case of double line river, contours are .............
options: stopped at the banks of the river
stopped at the edge of the river
drawn by parabolic curves having their vertex at the centre of the water
explain: For a double-line river, contours are drawn to the edge of the water but not across it, as the water surface itself is level.

q: 267. An imaginary line lying throughout on the surface of the earth and preserving a constant inclination to the horizontal, is called .............
explain: A contour gradient is a line that maintains a uniform slope or inclination with the horizontal.

q: 268. From any point on the surface with a given inclination .............
options: only one contour gradient is possible
explain: From a single point, you can go in two directions along the hillside to maintain a specific gradient.

q: 269. Location of contour gradient for a highway is best set out from .............
explain: Starting from a saddle or ridge allows the surveyor to work downwards and find the best alignment for a road gradient.

q: 270. An angle between the inclined line of sight and the horizontal is called .............
explain: A vertical angle is the angle measured in the vertical plane between the line of sight and the horizontal line.

q: 271. In locating the details of inaccessible objects visible at least from transit stations, the method used is .............
options: by angles and distances from the same station
by angle from one station and distance from the other station
by distances from two different stations
explain: Inaccessible objects are often located by observing angles from known stations (intersection method).

q: 272. The traversing by the method of deflection angles is chiefly used in .............
explain: Deflection angle traversing is standard for 'open' traverses like roads, railways, and canals where the route continues forward.

q: 273. The difference between the most probable value and its observed value is .............
explain: Residual error is the difference between the most probable value (MPV) and the actual measurement.

q: 274. An arbitrary surface with reference to which the elevation of points are measured and compared, is called .............
explain: The datum is the reference surface (like Mean Sea Level) from which heights or depths are measured.

q: 275. A line normal to the plumb line at all points is known as .............
explain: A level line follows the Earth's curvature and is perpendicular to the direction of gravity (plumb line) at every point.

q: 276. Substense bar is an instrument used for .............
options: measurement of horizontal distances in plane areas
measurement of horizontal distances in undulated areas
explain: A subtense bar is used in tacheometry to measure horizontal distances indirectly, which is particularly useful in rough or undulating terrain where chaining is difficult.

q: 277. The number of horizontal cross wires in a stadia diaphragm is .............
explain: A stadia diaphragm consists of one central horizontal cross-hair and two additional short horizontal hairs (stadia hairs) placed equidistantly above and below the center.

q: 278. A contour map of the area is essential before proceeding with the construction of .............
explain: For a dam project, a contour map is critical to calculate the reservoir capacity (volume), find the catchment area, and determine the best location for the spillway.

q: 279. Reciprocal leveling eliminates .............
options: collimation and curvature error fully and refraction error pertly
explain: By taking observations from both ends of a line, reciprocal leveling cancels out errors due to earth's curvature, atmospheric refraction (assuming it's constant), and imperfect adjustment of the line of collimation.

q: 280. Contour lines .............
explain: Contour lines must eventually close on themselves, either within the map limits or outside of them, as they represent a continuous path of equal elevation.

q: 281. Contour lines look to cross each other in case of .............
explain: In the case of an overhanging cliff, a higher contour line can physically overlap or 'cross' a lower contour line on a 2D map projection.

q: 282. In a theodolite the line of collimation is .............
options: parallel to axis of plate levels
explain: For a properly adjusted theodolite, the line of collimation (the optical axis) must be perpendicular to the horizontal (trunnion) axis.

q: 283. In a transit theodolite error due to eccentricity of verniers is counteracted by .............
options: reading different parts of main scale
taking both right swing and left swing reading
explain: Reading both verniers (A and B) and taking the mean value eliminates the error caused by the centers of the graduated circle and the alidade not coinciding.

q: 284. Right face and left reading are taken to .............
options: eliminate error of trunnion axis not exactly horizontal
eliminate error in the line of collimation
explain: Changing the face of the theodolite (Face Left and Face Right) eliminates errors due to the line of collimation not being perpendicular to the trunnion axis and the trunnion axis not being perpendicular to the vertical axis.

q: 285. Axis of altitude level is .............
options: parallel to the line of collimation
explain: The axis of the telescope level (altitude bubble) must be parallel to the line of collimation so that when the bubble is centered, the line of sight is horizontal.

q: 286. A 15 cm theodolite means .............
options: length of the telescope is 15 cm
diameter of lower plate is 15 cm
radius of upper plate is 15 cm
explain: The size of a theodolite is designated by the diameter of the graduated horizontal lower plate.

q: 287. A simple circular curve is designated by .............
options: angle subtended at the centre by a chord of any length
angle subtended at the centre by a chord of particular length
explain: In engineering practice, a curve is often designated by the degree of the curve, which is the angle subtended at the center by a standard chord (usually 20m or 30m).

q: 288. A fixed point of reference of known elevation is called .............
explain: A Bench Mark (BM) is a permanent or semi-permanent point of known elevation used as a reference for leveling.

q: 289. An imaginary line tangent to the longitudinal curve of the bubble tube at its middle points is called .............
explain: The axis of the level tube is the tangent to the inner surface of the bubble tube at its midpoint.

q: 290. The distances AC and BC are measured from two fixed points A and B whose distance AB is known. The point C is plotted by intersection. This method is generally adopted in .............
explain: Locating a point by measuring two linear distances from two known points is the fundamental principle of offset measurement in chain surveying.

q: 291. Mistakes which may produce a very serious effect upon the final results arise due to .............
explain: Unlike systematic errors, mistakes (blunders) are caused by human error such as misreading a tape or recording a value incorrectly.

q: 292. The systematic errors which persist and have regular effects in the performance of a survey operations, are due to .............
explain: Systematic errors (also called cumulative errors) follow a mathematical law and are often caused by faulty instrument adjustment (e.g., a tape that is too short).

q: 293. The method of reversal .............
options: is usually directed to examine whether a certain part is truly parallel or perpendicular to another
makes the erroneous relationship between parts evident
explain: Reversing the instrument (like face left/face right) doubles the instrumental error, making it clearly visible so it can be corrected or averaged out.

q: 294. The apparent error on reversal is .............
explain: When you reverse an instrument, the existing error is applied in the opposite direction, making the apparent gap between the two readings twice the actual error.

q: 295. The sensitivity of bubble tube can be increased by .............
options: decreasing the radius of curvature of tube
explain: Sensitivity increases with an increase in the internal diameter and the radius of curvature, and with a decrease in liquid viscosity.

q: 296. With the rise of temperature, the sensitivity of bubble tube .............
explain: When temperature rises, the liquid in the tube expands, causing the bubble length to decrease, which reduces the sensitivity of the tube.

q: 297. Refraction correction .............
options: has no effect on the curvature correction
explain: The refraction correction is negative (subtracts from staff reading) and the curvature correction is positive; since refraction is about 1/7 of curvature, it partially offsets it.

q: 298. While doing leveling in undulating terrain, it is preferable to set level on .............
explain: Setting the level on a side slope provides a clearer line of sight for both uphill and downhill points in hilly terrain.

q: 299. A leveling station is a place where .............
options: both B.S. and F.S. are taken
explain: In leveling terminology, a 'station' refers specifically to the location where the leveling staff is held, not where the instrument is placed.

q: 300. The telescope of a dumpy level .............
options: is rigidly fixed to the leveling head
can be tilted in a vertical plane
can be taken out of its supports and reversed
permits interchange of eye piece and object glass
explain: In a dumpy level, the telescope is rigidly fixed to its supports and cannot be rotated about its longitudinal axis or tilted vertically.
